summary: Wittgensteinian fideism (#1010) recorded in three variants from the pinned SEP entries Fideism §2.2.4 and Religious Language §§1, 4.1, 4.2: WF-N (critics' four theses), WF-P1 (early Phillips: religious belief expresses a moral vision, and praise does not refer to some object called God; the broader thesis that 'God' names no being is the unattributed STMT-GOD-NAMES-NO-BEING-WF-P1), WF-P2 (late Phillips and minimalism: reference and truth constituted inside the game, outside evidence admissible). Phillips, Winch and Nielsen themselves are in copyright with no hosted copy; bibliographic identities only, no claim read from them. Defeat by consequence of WF-N as a description of the Catholic practice: with Dei Filius can. II.1 (stated), the open bridge that conciliar definitions are the practice's own standards, and the open shared-reason reading of 'naturali humanae rationis lumine', the fideist pair is inconsistent (WF-FAILS-AS-DESCRIPTION-OF-CATHOLIC-PRACTICE); each premise is needed and the bundle alone is consistent (WF-CONSISTENT). Rejected: treating the defeat as a refutation of fideism in general, or of Phillips's 'not generally' thesis, which allows natural knowability; treating Nielsen's insulation charge as a defeat (it judges a consequence unacceptable, #1007). Self-application of the fideist thesis is recorded in prose only: the generic schema STMT-SELF-APPLICATION-DILEMMA applies, but the needed premise that the thesis lies outside the religious game is a judgment without vocabulary.
blocker: The defeat counts only once its three premises are established (#999); the definition bridge and the shared-reason reading are open, and the fideist's escapes are exactly their denials. The early-Phillips non-reference rival on the nominal-definition leaves is unrefuted (needs a typed reference relation and the Dei Filius ch. 1 / can. I.1-3 parallel).
